description: The HUS Group (also "the contracting entity", "the Client" or “HUS”) requests tenders for a large cancer panel test for HUS Diagnostic Center. The procurement includes also data analysis software for reporting clinically significant variants, copy number alterations and gene fusions. The software can be offered by the same provider as the large cancer panel test or from a partner company (offer as a group or appeal to a subcontractor's resources), but it needs to be included in the same tender. The software will be procured for the entire lifecycle of the assay. The procurement consist of gene panels and reagents (also "products") and data analysis software (also "services", e.g. information system provided as Software as a Service). Laboratory of Genetics at HUS (Helsinki University Hospital) Diagnostic Center is an SFS-EN ISO 15189:2022 accredited laboratory providing diagnostic genetic testing services to all patients at Helsinki and Uusimaa Hospital District. The laboratory operates as a health institution capable of validating in-house developed tests as required by the CE-IVD regulation. The services include analysis of both constitutional samples and malignancies. The laboratory provides sequencing services mainly using local sequencing capacity (Illumina NovaSeq 6000, NovaSeq X Plus, Ion GeneStudio S5 Prime equipment). The large cancer panel test is intended for detection of small nucleotide variants (SNVs), indels, gene fusions, copy number variations (CNVs), microsatellite instability (MSI), homologous recombination deficiency (HRD), and tumor mutation burden (TMB) relevant for the genetic profiling of solid tumor samples and/or hematological malignancies as well as plasma samples for cfDNA analysis. Sequencing of the samples is carried out using Illumina NovaSeq sequencers (Illumina NovaSeq 6000 and NovaSeq X Plus). The number of cancer panel tests performed annually is estimated to be between 2500-3000. The procurement is divided into LOT A and LOT B: LOT A - This lot includes gene panel solutions for in-house NGS testing of solid tumors and hematological malignancies, including library preparation reagents, target enrichment reagents defining the panel content, panel-specific reagents, data analysis software, and instructions for use. Sequencing reagents, flow cells, sequencing instruments, and testing services are not included in this procurement. - This test is based on analysis of total nucleic acids (RNA and/or DNA) extracted from paraffin embedded specimens and/or fresh-frozen specimens - This lot includes an option for special gene panel and reagents for salivary gland tumors with data analysis software - This lot includes an an option for a custom gene panel and reagents with data analysis software - The HUS Group will decide separately on the use of the options LOT B Important Information Concerning Lot B of the Procurement Procedure The Contracting Authority has decided to discontinue Lot B of the procurement procedure.During the procurement procedure, it became apparent that substantial amendments are required to the subject matter of Lot B and the related procurement documents. As these amendments cannot be implemented through a corrigendum without jeopardising the equal and non-discriminatory treatment of tenderers, the Contracting Authority has decided to discontinue Lot B.Lot B will be re-tendered through a separate procurement procedure. A new contract notice and new procurement documents for Lot B will be published separately.Please note that LOT A is still continuing the tendering process. - This lot includes gene panel solutions for in-house NGS testing of cell-free DNA, including library preparation reagents, target enrichment reagents defining the panel content, panel-specific reagents, data analysis software, and instructions for use. Sequencing reagents, flow cells, sequencing instruments, and testing services are not included in this procurement - This test is based on analysis of cell-free DNA from plasma samples NOTE: For LOT A, the tenderer may offer a catalog panel, a combination of catalog panels, or a custom solution to meet the DNA and RNA requirements. For hematological malignancies, only a panel for DNA is requested. Panel for salivary gland tumors and custom panel are requested as an option. NOTE: FOR LOT A and LOT B, the tender needs to include all the reagents required to perform the assay, including library preparation reagents, indexing adapters and target enrichment reagents (or equivalent). Nucleic acid extraction reagents, library quantification reagents and sequencer reagents are excluded from the tender. The subject of the procurement and its requirements are described in more detail in the call for tender and its appendices. The tenderer can submit a tender to either one or both of the LOTS A and LOT B. The tenderer can be awarded the contract to either one or both tendered lots. The contrcting entity selects one (1) supplier for each lot and will enter into an agreement with the winning supplier. The estimated start for the contract period is autumn-winter 2026. The contracting entity recieves a right to test use tendered panels and softwares after the deadline for receiving the tenders. The procurement volumes presented in the call for tenders are estimates, and the contract does not constitute a mandatory purchase obligation for the contrcting entity or an exclusive right for the supplier to provide the product.

title: Platform for the administration and distribution of digital teaching aids and learning tools.
description: Background and purpose Arendal is located in the central part of Sørlandet. The municipality has approx. 46,000 inhabitants. Arendal municipality has a decentralised school structure with 16 municipal primary and secondary schools, organised as independent entities with separate rectors and management groups. The schools include both combined 1st - 10th schools and pure primary schools (1st - 7th years), as well as a resource centre with tenders across the stages. The municipality has a total of approx. 5,000 pupils in the primary and lower secondary schools. Arendal municipality is in an ongoing change of the school structure. Two primary schools (1st – 7th years) and the secondary school for one school have been decided to be folded. The changes are planned to be implemented from 01.01.2027. The overall responsibility for the school area is at the school office, which follows up on joint priorities, quality work and regulations, and acts as a link between the political level and the schools. The cooperation between the school office and the schools will take place, among other things, through fixed meeting points and joint development work, at the same time that each school adapts the work to local needs. The adult education is organised as a part of the municipality ́s training and is also a user of relevant digital services. Arendal municipality needs a joint system for the administration, distribution and access management of digital teaching aids in primary and secondary schools. The municipality has used a system for this purpose over time and has developed good experience with procurement, licence management and access management in this area. The procurement will be carried out as a result of the expiry of the existing agreement and shall ensure the continuation and further development of this work. Information on the procurement and process is in the document Konkurransegrunnlag_Digital Platform for schools. Scope The estimated annual scope is challenging to estimate. This is connected with the complexity, changes in the school structure and a market with different actors. We estimate that the annual turnover will be NOK 3.0 million excluding VAT, which over 8 years will be NOK 24 million excluding VAT. The contract will have a valid amount of NOK 30 million excluding VAT during the contract period. The estimated scope is based on experiences with the current supplier, market dialogue and indicative prices in the market. The estimated scope is not binding for the contracting authority. The following is not included in this procurement: - Learning platform (LMS) and educational follow-up. - functionality connected to artificial intelligence (KI) - other school administrative systems. The procurement is for the administration and distribution of digital teaching aids and a learning tool. Handling printed teaching aids is not included. The procurement does not include discipline specific teaching aids or individual applications. Reservations All conditions that the tenderer has for the tender shall be stated in the point conditions in the requirement specification document. Alternative tenders Alternative tenders cannot be submitted. Documents Please see the attached documents. Note that the tenderer shall fill in information in the attached documents.

title: ESPON ARISE - Adaptive Resilience and Inclusive Strategies for Europe’s Structurally Declining Territories
description: The project will develop a coherent framework for understanding how territorial cohesion and resilience operate under conditions of persistent low growth, demographic contraction and structural decline. Based on European-wide territorial mapping, it will elaborate typologies of territories facing persistent low growth and demographic contraction, and produce territorial maps of vulnerability, adaptive capacity and resilience. Through comparative qualitative case studies across different territorial contexts, it will document adaptive territorial practices and governance innovations. Finally, the project will offer practical policy guidance suggesting how cohesion policy, territorial governance and resilience planning frameworks may need to evolve in response to persistent low growth and structural territorial contraction.

title: Dynamic purchasing system for passenger cars and goods vans.
description: Background Namsos municipality invites tenderers to participate in a competition for the establishment of a dynamic purchasing system (DIO) for the procurement of vehicles under 3.5 tons. The financial plan states that the fleet shall be rolled over within a frame of approx. NOK 4 million per annum. A dynamic procurement system is established to ensure a simple and flexible procurement process. This gives the contracting authority the possibility to hold simplified competitions with a ten day tender deadline for one or several vehicles. This has been requested by actors in the automotive industry, as reservation of cars over several weeks in connection with traditional tender competitions makes it difficult for suppliers to participate. The new scheme gives tenderers a better opportunity to participate, which is expected to give the municipality a better offer. About Dynamic Purchasing System The dynamic purchasing system will be established in accordance with the Public Procurement Regulations (FOA) part I and part III and it will be carried out as a restricted tender contest, cf. the Public Procurement Regulations § 26-5. The scheme is a two-stage procedure: Stage 1: Qualification phase, in which tenderers apply for admission to the scheme. Stage 2: Implementation of mini-competitions, in which qualified tenderers are invited to submit tender offers. A contract will not be signed for admission to the scheme. The contract will only be signed after a completed competition for each procurement. The scheme is fully electronic, and all communication and tender deliveries shall be carried out via the contracting authority ́s competition tool. Tenderers can apply for admission to the scheme by submitting a qualification application with ESPD. The scheme is open for continuous admissions: New suppliers can apply for admission throughout the entire scheme period. Applications are processed continuously All tenderers who fulfil the qualification requirements will be included in the scheme. Description of the delivery The dynamic purchasing system includes the purchase of passenger cars and goods vans. The scheme shall be used for ongoing procurements for the entire duration of the scheme. The estimated value over 10 years is NOK 40 million. It may be necessary to procure both passenger cars and goods vans and the need can vary in regard to i.a. size, capacity and other qualities. Service and follow-up of the vehicles is a part of the delivery. It is therefore a requirement that the tenderer is an authorised branded dealer and has his own workshop approved by the Norwegian Public Roads Administration. Implementation of competitions in the scheme The contracting authority will hold mini-competitions for concrete procurements, in which: All qualified tenderers are invited to submit a tender. The requirement specifications and contract terms will be determined in each competition. The award will be based on the criteria stated in the competition. The award criteria will normally include: Price Technical and functional quality Service and follow-up Delivery time The tender deadline in mini competitions will normally not be shorter than ten days. Other conditions There are requirements for wages and working conditions in accordance with the current rules. The contracting authority reserves the right to reject tenderers who do not fulfil the qualification requirements, or that are covered by the rejection regulations in PPR § 24-2. Information subject to client confidentiality will be processed in accordance with the current rules.

title: Framework agreement for winter maintenance in limited port areas.
description: Background The Port of Bergen needs to establish a new framework agreement for winter maintenance in a limited port area. Winter preparedness is necessary to ensure safe access and safe operation in the port area throughout the winter season. The area includes traffic and operational critical areas where weather and driving conditions can change quickly, and where measures can be implemented at short notice. The procurement shall facilitate clear interaction, effective handling of events connected to snow and ice, as well as ongoing coordination between the parties. Description of the assignment The assignment is for the provision of winter maintenance services in a limited area under the Bergen Port ́s area of responsibility. The service shall support safe and appropriate accessibility in the winter season and it will be controlled through a zone/route division with the accompanying level of execution, cf. annex 1a. Tenderers are expected to be able to clear several areas simultaneously as needed under heavy precipitation conditions. The delivery mainly includes snow clearing, snow shovelling and measures against slippery lead, including salting and/or gritting. If needed, the tenderer shall also be able to handle the removal of snow when local storage possibilities are inadequate. The assignment includes winter stand-by with a duty scheme and an option for emergency responses to events, so that the necessary measures can be carried out in connection with varying weather and driving conditions. The framework agreement shall support efficient interaction between the parties, including notification, ongoing coordination, simple documentation and reporting connected to completed assignments as a basis for follow-up and control. The Port of Bergen would like a pro-active supplier.

description: The aim of the procurement is to establish a framework agreement for the delivery of equipment, consumables and  production services for the production of standardised brands for locations and equipment in Helse Sør. East.  The procurement shall support the implementation and use of uniform physical and digital identification of  locations and equipment based on international GS1 standards. Locations shall be able to be identified by  use of GS1 GLN and the equipment shall be able to be identified by use of GS1 GIAI, in the form of GS1 Digital Link and  other standardised GS1 syntaxes. Through the use of international standards, marks shall be able to  be used by digital systems in Helse Sør-Øst, e.g. systems for Facility Management  (FM)/property management, clinical logistics, medical engineering, ERP, etc.   The procurement shall result in:  - Standardised types of brands for locations and equipment.   - Support for multiple information carriers on brands   - Support for local production of brands   - Support for production of large volumes of brands as external services.  - Standardised production basis.   - Secure management of business critical information. South Africa has significant potential to develop competitive green hydrogen and PtX industries due to its renewable energy resources, existing infrastructure, industrial base and potential domestic and international markets. At the same time, the country has significant potential to develop sustainable battery value chains, building on its established automotive industry and access to critical raw materials. The project provides support to public and private stakeholders to create an enabling policy and regulatory environment, strengthen capacities, improve the bankability of projects and develop sustainable and inclusive value chains. Its areas of work include strategy, policy and regulatory frameworks; private sector cooperation and finance; capacity strengthening, research and development; sustainability and just transition; and battery value chains. To respond flexibly and efficiently to the diverse and evolving demand for specialised expertise, GIZ intends to establish a framework agreement with an expert pool. The framework will enable the rapid mobilisation of qualified international and local experts for individual assignments addressing specific technical, economic, financial, environmental, social, regulatory, certification and battery value-chain related needs.

title: Digital system for registering cleaning and deviations.
description: Background Troms County (TFK) manages buildings of 218,000 m², comprising i.a. schools, sports facilities, dental clinics, workplaces and other county buildings. The cleaning services are carried out by approx. 130 cleaners organised by teams, with a focus on flexible work forms, efficient use of resources and quality in the service delivery. The County municipality needs a more uniform, digital and documentable follow-up of cleaning across buildings, rooms and areas. The current systems do not provide sufficient support for registration and follow-up of work performed, deviations and quality measurements. Therefore there is a need for a system that makes it easy for cleaners to register work and register conditions that affect cleaning, for example rooms that cannot be cleaned, deviations or a lack of periodic cleaning. At the same time, the county needs a better overview and management information. Managers should be able to follow the status per building, area and room, identify areas that have not been cleaned and get a better basis for planning capacity, resource use and absence management. The cleaning quality shall be measured and documented in accordance with NS-INSTA 800. TFK would like systems that provide good support for quality follow-up, reporting and analysis, which contribute to increased user friendliness, better decision making and more efficient operation. The procurement is being made to establish a future orientated digital system that provides a better overview, more uniform practice, better documentation and more efficient management of deviations, quality follow-up and resource planning. Description of the assignment The assignment includes the delivery, establishment, operation and support of a digital cleaning system for Troms County. The system shall provide an overview of cleaning per building, room and area and it can be used by cleaners, substitutes, managers, administrators and operations managers where the work is carried out. The system shall support planning, implementation, documentation and follow-up of the cleaning services. The system shall, among other things: Give easy registration of completed cleaning, status and deviations. Support registration and follow-up of periodic cleaning. Give an overview of rooms and areas that have not been cleaned or where deviations are registered. Support quality measurements and documentation in accordance with NS-INSTA 800. Offer reports and management information that supports follow-up, documentation, analysis and resource planning. Support both short term and long term planning of assignments and resources. Be able to integrate with existing and future MOM systems, as well as facilitate future integrations with other support systems, including possibilities for future use of sensor technology, such as dispensers, waste handling, machines and robots. The delivery shall include the necessary establishment and configuration of the building and room structure, user roles and access management, as well as training, user support and administrative assistance in connection with the introduction and use of the system. TFK would like a user friendly and visually oriented system that facilitates efficient operation, good quality control and future development of the cleaning services. Further requirements for functionality, technical conditions, security, privacy, integrations and service level are stated in the requirement specification.

title: SPR/260834 - Provision of genomic epidemiology and public health bioinformatics training
description: The overall objective of this tender is to procure a Framework Contract to strengthen the capacity for genomic epidemiology and public health bioinformatics through interdisciplinary trainings, which is crucial for response during a pandemic or unexpected major public health events. The general objectives of the trainings are to support countries in building up their capacity in genomic epidemiology and bioinformatics for public health purposes, and to increase the interdisciplinary collaboration between bioinformaticians, epidemiologists and microbiologists within a country to facilitate the routine use of genomic information for surveillance, preparedness, and outbreak response. Activities shall also enhance data sharing and collaborations between public health institutions and ECDC, and enhanced networking activities will foster cross-border collaborations. The target groups for the trainings are professionals working in public health institutions with a background in computational biology and bioinformatics; and professionals working in public health institutions who do not have a specific background in bioinformatics. The aims of the trainings are: * To allow the professionals with a background in computational biology and bioinformatics to: - enhance and extend their skills in order to strengthen their capacity in the field of public health bioinformatics; - better understand the needs and concepts of epidemiology and public health microbiology, with a focus on the inputs and outputs needed by their counterparts (i.e. microbiologists, epidemiologists, professionals in public health surveillance and response) to take rapid and informed public health action. * To allow the professionals without a background in computational biology/bioinformatics to: - gain a better understanding of how genomic epidemiology can be applied in a public health context with special focus on how traditional and genomic data can be jointly analysed, interpreted and used for public health purposes; - become more familiar with the concepts, formats and conventions commonly used in microbial genomics, and get a better understanding of how the structure and format of the data can be used to streamline the data analysis process; - better understand the concepts behind and use of the most common bioinformatic tools and pipelines used for epidemiological analyses, including limitations and possible alternatives; and - gain a better overview of the basic principles, options for and best practices of data storage, management and sharing, with a specific focus on sequencing data and associated metadata.

title: Copenhagen - New Metroline, M5 Civil Works South
description: This tender presents a substantial opportunity for prospective contractors to bid for the M5 Civil Works South (CWS) package, an important component of the Copenhagen metro system's expansion. This project is of significant strategic importance, as the M5 line is a fully automated driverless metro system that will not only enhance passenger service on existing metro corridors but also extend connectivity to emerging urban development areas, including Kløverparken, Refshaleøen, and Lynetteholm in the East Harbour. The M5 is designed to operate as an independent system, ensuring that its construction and subsequent operation do not disrupt the existing M1-M4 metro lines. MAIN COMPONENTS OF THE M5 CIVIL WORK The M5 south consists of approx 6.5 km twin bored TBM tunnels, 5 underground stations (incl. 3 transfer stations), 2 underground crossovers, 1 shaft, 5 cross passages, 1 ramp, approx 2.0 km viaduct, 1 elevated station, 1 viaduct cross-over, 1 elevated bifurcation, short embankment sections. For further details on scope ref. is made to M5-2.1-CMBS-SW and M5-2.2-CWS-SW PHASES: The current tender, Phase 1, encompasses the southern section of the line, from north-west of København H to north of v/Prags Boulevard, with an anticipated operational commencement in 2036. The broader vision includes phase 2 north of v/Prags Boulevard to Lynetteholm opening in 2045 and a potential future extension to form a ring line, signifying a long-term commitment to urban mobility. Phase 2 is not included in this tender. CONTRACT SPLIT OF M5: The M5 project as a whole consists of several contracts: • M5 Civil Works South (this contract) • M5 Transportation System South contract (tendered out as a separate contract in June 2026) • Operation and Maintenance contract (will be tendered out at a later stage) • Enabling Works contracts, e.g. relocation of utilities, relocation works at Kh etc. (enabling works will be tendered out in separate contracts) • Station and Shaft areas (will be tendered out at a later stage) • Canopy contracts (will be tendered out at a later stage). CONTRACT The contract is structured as a design & build contract under ABT18 terms, placing comprehensive responsibility for both design and execution upon the Contractor. This two-phase approach—design followed by execution—is a standard framework for complex infrastructure projects. A market dialogue has been carried out before issuing the tender. The purpose of the market dialogue was to ensure that the project is attractive to the market, and to ensure competitive and compliant final tenders to be used as basis for the award of contract. Metroselskabet I/S is grateful for the potential tenderers who took their time to participate in the dialogue and provided input. INDICATIVE TIMESCHEDULE FOR THE PROCUREMENT Publication of contract notice September 10th 2026. Publication of tender documentation September 11th 2026. Deadline for submission of application for prequalification October 13th 2026, ref. made to section 5.1.12. Dialogue phase November 2026-October 2027. Final tender November 2027. Award of contract December 2027. The time-schedule may be subject to change.

title: ENEST regional communication programme (2027-2031)
description: The European Union's engagement with partner countries has gained renewed strategic importance in response to the evolving geopolitical environment and the renewed momentum of the enlargement process. The programme covers partner countries at different stages of their relationship with the European Union, requiring communication approaches that reflect their respective political contexts, policy priorities and communication needs. Communication challenges differ by the fact that public awareness of the European Union's support remains uneven across the region. While the European Union is the largest donor, investor and trading partner for most partner countries, public understanding of the scale and impact of EU support, as well as of the accession process itself, remains limited. Recent perception surveys carried out under the regional communication programmes show that many citizens are insufficiently informed about the European Union's policies, financial assistance and priorities. Against this background, strategic communication has become an integral part of the European Union's engagement with partner countries. Previous regional communication programmes have successfully increased the visibility of the European Union, developed valuable communication tools and established networks of partners and multipliers across the region. The future programme will continue this effort and adopt a more strategic and service-oriented approach in supporting DG ENEST and EU Delegations communicating the European Union's priorities across partner countries. The programme will provide communication campaigns and products, strengthen engagement with key multipliers, improve the visibility of EU support, generate communication intelligence and audience insights, and offer flexible communication services that can be mobilised in response to operational needs. This approach will ensure greater coherence across partner countries while allowing communication activities to be adapted to national contexts and emerging geopolitical developments.

title: Contract for the purchase, leasing and operation of vehicles.
description: 1 General Description 1.1 About the Contracting Authority The contracting authority for this competition is Møre og Romsdal county, c/o the County Road Department. See the website [URL] for information on the Contracting Authority. 1.2 About the Assignment - the objective of the procurement 1.2.1 Purpose The contracting authority needs to enter into a contract with a supplier of vehicle administration. The procurement/agreement shall include both the purchase (new vehicle) and leasing (operational) of official vehicles as well as vehicle administration of official cars. The contracting authority needs a system that ensures a modern, economic, safe and environmentally friendly vehicle fleet as well as an intuitive administration of the fleet of vehicles. The chosen tenderer must also be an advisory and solution orientated cooperation partner. 1.2.2 Extent As stated in point 1.2.1, the contract shall include: 1. Purchase and leasing (operational) of official vehicles 2. Vehicle administration with travel log and fleet management (option). Delivery under point 1: As regards the procurement of a new vehicle under point 1, the competition concludes that tenders will not be submitted for concrete vehicle models, but on vehicle groups. The choice of a specific type of vehicle within the defined vehicle groups will be made when ordered during the contract period. Examples of vehicle types that will be ordered are in the price form, annex 4, tab 4. If the vehicle is procured, the tenderer shall act as a "communicator" where he collects tender offers based on predetermined procedures, cf. The assignment description annex point 1.1.2 Selection of vehicles/tenders is to be made by the contracting authority. The price of this service (facilitation) is an award per vehicle. There is a price for this communication fee that is being competed on. When leasing, suppliers offer vehicles within defined vehicle groups, where prices for leasing are calculated according to cost price, i.e. purchase price with deduction for discounts + specified equipment and possibly fittings. title: 10037895-Development of a National M&E System in Palestine
description: Description of the Project: Local Governance Reform Programme (LGRP) III The "Multi-Donor Action (EU-BMZ) - Strengthening Capacities and Institutional Readiness of Reform Actors in Palestine" co-financed by the European Union (EU) and the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH, aims to enhance the institutional capacity, operational effectiveness, and coordination functions of MoFP and PMO ERO as leading entities in national planning and reform management. The Action will support MoFP in its role as the central coordinating body for national planning by enhancing its capacity to embed data-driven policymaking, ensure coherent approaches across line ministries, and improve coordination across all levels of governance. The Palestinian Authority (PA) faces significant institutional and technical challenges in managing, measuring, and demonstrating public sector performance. Monitoring and evaluation (M&E) functions across line ministries and agencies (LMAs) are narrowly defined, fragmented, and largely disconnected from planning and budgeting decisions. Indicators are poorly formulated, feeder data is weak and uncoordinated, and M&E reporting serves administrative compliance rather than evidence-based management. The Strategic Results Framework (SRF), which is the principal instrument for measuring national results delivery, lacks a usable structure, theory of change, and coherent indicator set. No overarching national M&E strategy exists, and data management responsibilities across government institutions remain undefined and unanchored.

title: Dynamic Purchasing System for Sequencing Services for Human-Derived Biological Samples
description: The contracting authority establishes a Dynamic Purchasing System for sequencing services for human-derived biological samples. All suppliers meeting the suitability requirements will be admitted to the system. Individual procurements will be conducted through mini-competitions within the DPS. The procedure is fully electronic. This Dynamic Purchasing System covers sequencing and associated laboratory and bioinformatics services for human-derived biological samples. The DPS is platform-agnostic and includes services performed using commercially available sequencing, enrichment, and single-cell analysis technologies, such as but not limited to: Sequencing modalities Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS), Whole Exome Sequencing (WES) Targeted DNA and RNA sequencing (custom and standardized panels) RNA-seq (bulk), single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq ATAC-seq (bulk), single-cell and single-nucleus ATAC-seq ChIP-seq and chromatin-state profiling Hi-C and related genome conformation assays Sequencing platforms (non-exhaustive, non-binding examples) -Short-read sequencing platforms, including optical- and chemistry-based systems -Long-read sequencing platforms, including single-molecule real-time and nanopore-based systems -Capillary electrophoresis Sanger sequencing systems (e.g., platforms commonly represented by ABI 3730/3500 series or equivalent) -Two-color and novel chemistry short-read platforms (e.g., platforms comparable to AVITI or equivalent) Single-cell and enrichment systems (non-binding examples) -Microfluidics- and droplet-based single-cell workflows (e.g., platforms comparable to 10x Genomics Chromium or equivalent) -Hybrid capture and target enrichment kits/workflows (e.g., systems comparable to Twist Bioscience target capture or equivalent) The DPS also covers: -Sample reception, QC, and nucleic acid preparation -Library preparation and enrichment -Sequencing execution -Primary, secondary, and optional tertiary bioinformatics analysis -Secure data delivery and optional data archiving All platforms and workflows offered must be commercially validated, reproducible, and compliant with biosafety and data protection requirements for human-derived materials. Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) Operating Model A Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) is an entirely electronic procurement framework used to purchase goods, services, or works that are commonly available on the market. Unlike a traditional framework agreement, the DPS remains open for new suppliers to join at any time during its validity, as long as they meet the selection criteria. How the DPS Works: 1. Establishment of the DPS The contracting authority defines the procurement scope, requirements, and supplier qualification criteria. A contract notice is published, and the DPS is set up as an electronic system (e.g., in an e-procurement platform). No suppliers or prices are selected at this stage—only the system is created. 2. Supplier Admission Suppliers can apply to join the DPS at any point while the system is active. They submit evidence that they meet the predefined eligibility and capability requirements. Once verified, they are admitted to the DPS supplier pool. 3. Call-Off (Mini-Competition) Procedure When a specific need arises, the contracting authority: Defines the requirements for that individual procurement and Invites suppliers under the DPS to submit bids. A competitive bidding process follows, typically with simplified tender documentation. Minimum tendering period is 10 days in DPS and the exact object of the procurement is a case by case decision. 4. Evaluation and Contract Award Bids are evaluated based on the award criteria defined for that specific call-off. A contract is then awarded to the supplier offering the best value according to the evaluation. Evaluation criteria generally include (but not limited to): -Price 40–60% -Quality / protocols / turnaround time 40–60% 5. System Remains Open New suppliers may continue joining the DPS throughout its duration. Requirements and call-offs may be repeated as needed. There is no limit on the number of suppliers admitted.

description: The project "Integrated Territorial Development and Good Governance in Togo" is implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). It supports the Government of Togo in advancing decentralisation and territorial development in the regions of Kara and Savanes. Despite progress in decentralisation, regional and local authorities face persistent challenges in exercising transferred competences, delivering quality public services, mobilising local revenues and promoting inclusive local economic development. These constraints are compounded by poverty, climate change, demographic pressure and a fragile security context in northern Togo. The overall objective is to enable regional and local actors to harness the social and economic potential of their territories to improve living conditions in an equitable and sustainable manner. The project applies an integrated territorial development approach with capacity development at individual, organisational and institutional levels. It cooperates with national ministries (Ministry of Local Development, Ministry of Decentralisation, Ministry of Finance), regional councils and municipalities, the National Training Agency for Local Authorities (Agence nationale de formation des collectivités territoriales, ANFCT), the National Association of Municipalities (Faîtière des Communes du Togo, FCT), civil society organisations and private sector actors. To sustain decentralisation and territorialisation efforts, the project also aims at strengthening socio-economic resilience, in particular of communities in the Northen border regions, and provide economic perspectives, in particular for young people. Activities are structured around three complementary outputs: (1) Strengthening the capacities of regional and local authorities to implement transferred competences. (2) Improving collaboration between public institutions, local authorities, civil society and the private sector for inclusive and conflict-sensitive territorial development. (3) Strengthening transparent, participatory and accountable local public financial management. Innovative elements include municipal benchmarking, peer-to-peer learning, digital solutions for local governance, performance-based management and evidence-based decision-making. Gender equality, social inclusion (LNOB), climate resilience, conflict sensitivity and digitalisation are mainstreamed across all interventions to ensure sustainable and scalable results. The assignment targets 38 municipalities in Kara and Savanes through FCT and ANFCT, with a view to progressive replication towards all 117 municipalities. Benchmarking and peer learning will be designed, piloted and institutionalised to steer capacity development and foster continuous improvement. In addition, specialised technical assistance will complement these mechanisms across the three outputs, including support for implementing transferred competences, facilitating inclusive territorial collaboration and strengthening local public financial management (e. g. participatory budgeting, revenue mobilisation, transparency and anti-corruption), while ensuring digital solutions adhere to recognised standards and are interoperable with national ecosystems.

title: 10022598-Short-Term Expert Pools to support negotiations and implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)
description: Background: Although many of the world"s fastest-growing economies are in Africa, trade among African countries remains limited. The continent mostly exports raw materials and agricultural products, while it imports machinery, equipment, and food mainly from outside Africa. The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which is one of the African Union"s (AU) flagship projects for the implementation of its Agenda 2063, aims to change this. It is expected that, with the introduction of the free trade zone, intra- African trade will be 15% to 25% higher by 2040 (UNECA). The AfCFTA agreement has been signed by 54 of the 55 African Union Member States (MS) and became effective under international law in May 2019. The full implementation of the AfCFTA will lead to a continental single market of more than 1.4 billion people with an aggregate GDP exceeding USD 2 trillion. Our Approach: The GIZ implemented project "Support to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) II" cofinanced by the BMZ and the EU, seeks to improve framework conditions for the realisation of the AfCFTA and supports the outstanding negotiations and the implementation of the AfCFTA. For this, the programme supports the African Union, specifically the Department for Economic Development, Trade, Tourism, Industry, Minerals (ETTIM) and the AfCFTA Secretariat at the continental level in the coordination of AfCFTA implementation. On the regional level the programme cooperates with Regional Economic Communities (RECs), specifically EAC (East African Community), ECOWAS (Economic Community for West African States) and SADC (South African Development Community, plus additional RECs based on request). The programme also supports Member States (Ethiopia, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, Tunisia, Zambia, plus additional Member States based on request) by working with national institutions, like trade ministries and customs, to implement the agreement. Lastly, the programme works closely with private sector and civil society actors to increase trade under the AfCFTA. Together with the named partners, the programme covers interventions across all technical areas of the AfCFTA. The EU co-financed part of the programme, the EU Technical Assistance Facility, operates as a multi-partner contribution agreement between the European Commission, GIZ (lead implementing agency), Expertise France, and FIAP. A Project Management Unit, which is housed in the AfCFTA Secretariat, oversees the implementation of the programme and the execution of activities.

title: EU Complementary Time (C-T) and Complementary Position and Navigation (C-PN) services
description: Satellite-based navigation and timing services are a cornerstone of Europe’s economy and critical infrastructure resilience. Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) functions, delivered principally by Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) such as the EU owned Galileo, underpin sectors ranging from transport and finance to energy and telecommunications. Several studies attribute roughly 10 % of EU GDP to PNT related activities, while a single day without GNSS could have a financial impact up to €1 billion. The Commission proposal for the European Competitiveness Fund (ECF), includes for the 2028‑2034 Multi‑annual Financial Framework, a contribution to complementary PNT services, which shall increase the resilience in case of disruptions to the services provided by the PNT component (Article 59). The project shall assess how best can the Commission contribute to complementary PNT services in the next MFF. Leveraging existing national and pan‑European infrastructure, the Commission would like to assess: • How to best strengthen with the resilience of PNT services to radio frequency interference (RFI) affecting GNSS services throughout the EU. • How to best contribute to the deployment of a mature, interoperable C T architecture that is ready for operational use within the multi financial framework 2028 2034. • How to best support candidates for a C-PN service, that utilise the C-T infrastructure and are resilient to RFI and to assess whether the technology is ready for deployment or, if not what is required.

title: Airborne Maritime Pollution Surveillance
description: This tender concerns a contract for Airborne Maritime Pollution Surveillance. The overall purpose is to limit and mitigate pollution in the Danish waters — territorial sea and the Danish economic exclusive zone (as defined in the Danish act on Protection of the Marine Environment (in Danish: Havmiljøloven) section 5) by performing airborne maritime pollution control and to enforce the Danish act on Protection of the Marine Environment (in Danish: Havmiljøloven). Further information about the characteristics of the airborne maritime pollution control can be obtained from the following sources: — The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea; UNCLOS; — The Bonn-Agreement; — The Helsinki Convention (HELCOM); — The DENGERNETH Plan; — The SWEDENGER Plan; — The Copenhagen Agreement. The supplier enters this agreement with DALO as the contracting party, and the inherent tasks are performed by the Danish Defence. The responsibility for pollution response and counter-pollution surveillance of the marine environement rests with the Ministry of Resilience and Preparedness. As such, this agreement may be subject to transfer to the Ministry of Resilience and Preparedness or an agency under the Ministry's purview, such as the Danish Emergency Management Agency. The maritime pollution surveillance is conducted by airborne area coverage of the Danish waters and this is supplemented by satellite based surveillance by European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA). The Supplier of Airborne Maritime Pollution Surveillance shall overfly areas within the Danish waters — territorial sea and the Danish economic exclusive zone (as defined in the Danish act on Protection of the Marine Environment section 5) two times weekly. The flights shall take place both at day time and at night time and under all weather conditions of common occurrence in the respective areas. Flights will be scheduled by the Supplier. During the flights the Danish waters shall be monitored with the purpose of identifying prospective pollution. Monitoring shall be conducted by means of sensor equipment, which is capable of monitoring the water surface for oil spill etc. The sensor equipment must be made available by the Supplier. During the flights the Supplier shall collect evidence of any observed pollution, hereunder by photo and other documentation and by means of air-drop of oil spill sampling buoys, with the purpose of for example giving the Danish Authorities information to assess the measures to be taken in combating the pollution and providing evidence for further investigation and/or preliminary charges. Specifically the Supplier shall provide the following for airborne maritime pollution surveillance: — Flight system; — sensor equipment; — air crew and system operators necessary for operating flight system and sensor equipment. The Supplier must prior to commencement undertake extensive practical training of his air crew and system operators. The Supplier must ensure that the system operators are at all times duly qualified and trained to perform the task. The Supplier shall be available for participation in multinational operations on behalf of Denmark. The number of such operations is expected to be up to three per year. Participation in such operations is comparable to the flights as described above. The Supplier shall be available/stand by for the duration of these operations.

title: Temporary compound tradesman services

title: Multi-Party Framework for Port Hydrographic Survey Works
description: DPC intends to establish a multi-party framework for Port Hydrographic Survey Works, to: a. provide hydrographic, geophysical, and associated marine survey services across DPC’s operational and capital programme requirements; b. support DPC in fulfilling its statutory duties as a client in respect of health and safety coordination during the design process, across a range of civil, structural, marine, building and infrastructure projects throughout the framework term. Framework Members shall be capable of providing, as a minimum, the following survey services whether in-house or through an approved consortium: DPC requires firms with strong health and safety design coordination experience across a range of construction project types, including civil engineering, marine structures, port infrastructure, buildings, and utilities works. A. Core Survey Services Non-Exhaustive The required expertise includes, but is not limited to: • Multi-Beam EchoSounder MBES monitoring surveys of all navigation channels, berth facilities, docks, and anchorage areas; • MBES measurement surveys in association with capital and maintenance dredging works, including pre-, interim, and post-dredge surveys; • Assessment of seabed characteristic information from backscatter returns where MBES equipment is used; • Single-Beam EchoSounder SBES monitoring surveys where required, particularly at Dundalk Port and in shallow areas; • Assistance with archaeological and obstruction identification, including geophysical, magnetometer, side scan sonar SSS, and drop-down video DDV services; • Acquisition of intertidal areas and adjacent structures using LIDAR-based methods; • Establishment of new and existing berth fender lines and quay features; • Calibration and validation of port tide gauges and tide boards; • Establishment and/or validation of temporary benchmarks; • Provision of post-processing, quality control, and data management, including delivery of survey data in agreed formats XYZ, LAS, CARIS, PDF, and other formats as required; • Preparation of survey reports, cross-sections, contour plots, and comparison overlays to DPC’s requirements. • Professional indemnity, marine liability, and other insurances in the amounts required under the Framework Agreement. B. Additional Services In addition to the core survey services set out above, DPC may require Framework Members to provide the following additional services under individual call-off contracts: Additional services may include non-exhaustive: • Sub-bottom profiling surveys; • Wreck investigation and obstruction surveys; • Geotechnical sampling support positioning and data integration; • Assistance with environmental monitoring surveys suspended sediment, turbidity, etc.; • GNSS/RTK control network establishment and verification; BIM and GIS integration and delivery of survey data to DPC’s asset management systems. Candidates should note that this list is non-exhaustive, and the successful tenderer may be required to provide other survey services as requested by DPC during the Framework. Important: DPC seeks only Candidates capable of delivering all core services listed in Section 3.1A, whether in-house or through a consortium/grouping. Applications limited to one or more survey types only may be rejected.

title: Policy Dialogue and Public Diplomacy Facility for Canada
description: The purpose of this procurement is to procure services that strengthen and deepen EU–Canada relations on key priority themes of shared strategic interest, while advancing EU interests and values in Canada through targeted policy dialogue and public diplomacy. The contract will support the implementation of commitments under the EU–Canada Strategic Partnership Agreement (SPA), the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), and, where relevant, other bilateral frameworks including the EU–Canada Green Alliance and the EU–Canada Security and Defence Partnership. The procured services shall comprise two complementary components: Policy Dialogue Support — facilitation of structured policy dialogues across a wide range of areas through concrete activities linked to existing and emerging dialogue mechanisms, including joint committees and working groups involving the EU Delegation and relevant EU services. Public Diplomacy Actions — Design and delivery of public diplomacy initiatives aimed at increasing understanding of EU policies and priorities among Canadian audiences, demonstrating the tangible benefits of the EU–Canada partnership, and strengthening engagement with key Canadian stakeholders beyond government — including media, academia, civil society, youth, and opinion leaders. The services shall deliver measurable policy outcomes, consolidate trusted stakeholder networks, and amplify EU positions across Canada. Through the combined effect of policy dialogue and public diplomacy, the procurement aims to enhance the visibility and credibility of the EU in Canada and contribute to closer alignment between EU and Canadian policy positions and approaches, including in multilateral fora, on major foreign policy priorities.

title: Provision of Relocation, Move Support, Warehousing and Distribution Services for the European Union Agency for Asylum (EUAA) premises in Malta Lot1: Relocation and Move Support Services Malta Lot2: Warehousing and Distribution Services Malt
description: The European Union Agency for Asylum (EUAA) requires the provision of Relocation and Move Support Services (Lot 1) and Warehousing and Distribution Services (Lot 2) in Malta as described in Part 2 – Technical Specifications. The services are necessary to support the Agency’s operational, administrative and logistical activities, including internal relocations within EUAA premises and relocations between different EUAA premises in Malta., the handling and transport of furniture, office equipment, archives and other assets, as well as the storage and distribution of palletised and non-palletised goods. The procurement has been structured into two Lots in order to ensure that relocation and move support services, and warehousing and distribution services, can be managed independently while remaining under the same procurement procedure. Under Lot 1, the required services include, inter alia: • Supply of packaging materials and crate rental/delivery services, with due regard to environmental performance requirements • Organisation, coordination and execution of relocation and move support activities, including dismantling and reassembly of furniture and equipment • Provision of qualified personnel (e.g. Move Manager, Foreman, porters and specialised staff), including, where requested, permanent porter services during EUAA working hours • Provision of appropriate vehicles and handling equipment suitable for small, medium and large-scale relocation operations Under Lot 2, the services include: • Secure storage of palletised and non-palletised goods, calculated in accordance with the Financial Tender Form • Inbound handling operations (receiving, unloading, palletisation, labelling, inspection and placement into storage) • Outbound handling operations (picking, packing, reconfiguration and loading) • Transportation services for inbound and outbound movements, including dedicated vehicles and after-hours transport, where required Given the dynamic and occasionally urgent nature of EUAA’s operations, the Agency must ensure access to reliable, flexible and professional service providers capable of responding to ad-hoc requests, short notice operations and fluctuating volumes. The availability of these services is essential to guarantee business continuity, safeguard EUAA assets, ensure compliance with health and safety and environmental requirements, and maintain operational efficiency across all EUAA premises in Malta.

title: Tipperary County Council Procurement of Single-Party Framework Agreement for Architect-Led Integrated Design Team Consultancy Services for Clonmel, Co. Tipperary
description: Tipperary County Council Procurement of Single-Party Framework Agreement for Architect-Led Integrated Design Team Consultancy Services for Clonmel, Co. Tipperary. Tipperary County Council is undertaking a competitive tendering process for the establishment of a Single-Party Framework Agreement for Architect-Led Integrated Multi-Disciplinary Consultancy Services for Public Realm, Landscape and Building Upgrade Projects in Clonmel, Co. Tipperary. The Framework Agreement will require the successful Consultant to provide, either directly or through its proposed multi-disciplinary team, all of the following services: 1. Architectural Services – Public Realm 2. Conservation Architectural Services 3. Landscape Architectural Services 4. Civil and Structural Engineering Services 5. Quantity Surveying Services 6. Project Management Services 7. Project Supervisor Design Process (PSDP) Services 8. Employer’s Representative Services 9. Public Liaison / Stakeholder Engagement Services 10. Mechanical and Electrical Engineering Services 11. Planning Services 12. Archaeological Services 13. Fire Engineering Services Only Applicants capable of providing all of the above disciplines and associated specialist expertise, whether in-house, through subcontractors or as part of a grouping/consortium, will be considered. This competition will be conducted using a restricted procedure. At Stage 1, Applicants will be assessed against the suitability and selection criteria set out in the Suitability Assessment Questionnaire. It is intended that the five highest-scoring Applicants, subject to a sufficient number meeting all minimum requirements and rules for selection, will be invited to participate in Stage 2. At Stage 2, shortlisted Applicants will be issued with the Invitation to Tender and associated tender documentation. Tenders will be evaluated in accordance with the award criteria and weightings set out in the Invitation to Tender. The highest-ranked compliant Tenderer will be appointed to the Single-Party Framework Agreement and will also be awarded the Initial Contract. The Initial Contract will relate to the further development and delivery of public realm and associated projects in Clonmel. Clonmel Town Centre requires a significant streetscape and public realm upgrade. A design previously received Part VIII approval; however, the design now requires further development, amendment and coordination to reflect the current project scope and available funding and to bring the project through detailed design, tender, construction and handover stages. Tipperary County Council has also acquired a protected structure for which design development and a Part VIII planning process will be required. The Architect-Led Design Team may therefore be required to deliver a combination of public realm, landscape, civil engineering and building upgrade works, including works to protected and heritage structures. The Architect will act as Lead Consultant and will be responsible for coordinating and managing the full multi-disciplinary design team, programme, cost and delivery of the projects. During the construction stage, the Design Team will be required to provide ongoing technical support, respond to queries arising on site and advise on proposed variations and other matters affecting the delivery of the works. Projects arising under the Framework Agreement are anticipated to be funded, in whole or in part, through the Towns and Cities Regeneration Investment Fund (TCRIF) and/or other available funding programmes. Please note that an ITT is not required for this stage of the tender process.

title: VR-Group/ Web development expert services, framework agreement
description: The objective of this procurement is to establish a multi-supplier framework agreement for the provision of software development expertise for the entire VR Group. The framework covers development needs arising across VR Group companies, including but not limited to passenger services, logistics operations, infrastructure-related systems, commercial platforms, customer-facing digital services, and internal operational systems. The procurement covers Web Development (e.g. web based technologies such as modern frontend frameworks and standards). Experts are assigned to VR’s agile development teams, who operate according to VR’s technology choices and established models where VR acts as the Product Owner and oversees overall project and development management. Work is carried out in a hybrid model, both on-site at VR’s premises in Helsinki and remotely in accordance with VR’s working guidelines. The service also includes a Supplier-appointed Service Manager (for reporting, invoicing etc.). In accordance with Section 45(2) of the Act on Procurement in the Utilities Sectors, the maximum total value of contracts awarded under this Framework Agreement during the entire contract period shall be EUR 20 000 000 (VAT 0%). Tenderers are requested to note that the value stated above does not constitute the estimated value of the procurement, but the statutory maximum value as referred to in the Act. The maximum value also includes possible option periods of the procurement. VR Group does not commit to any minimum purchase volumes. Actual resource needs may increase or decrease during the contract period based on business requirements, technological development, and the lifecycle of projects and systems. The initial contract period is two (2) years, after which the Customer may extend the Agreement with four (4) optional periods of one (1) year each. This procurement will be carried out using an open procedure. The Finnish Act on Procurements and Concession Contracts of Entities Operating in the Water and Energy Supply, Transport and Postal Services Sector (Act 1398/2016, “Act on Public Contracts in the Utilities Sector”) applies to this procurement. Tenders must meet all suitability requirements set out in this notice and its appendices. The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in Appendix 2 (Procurement Description) to the Invitation to Tender. The suitability requirements for Tenderers are set out in the ESPD form.

title: 10009293-Development of inclusive financial services and products
description: Iraq faces a persistent gap between its people and the financial system. Banks have long leaned on large state-owned institutions, credit has flowed mainly to established borrowers, and micro and small businesses along with women entrepreneurs and displaced communities have been largely left out. ProDIGI project, full name Promoting Employment in the Digital and Green Economy in Iraq, is trying to change that in a practical, grounded way. ProDIGI is a multi-donor initiative commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), co-financed by the European Union, and implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH. The project covers central and southern Iraq as well as the Kurdistan Region, with a focus on areas where joblessness, displacement, and limited access to services overlap. Within the project, Output 3 targets the financial inclusion side of the challenge. The starting point is a clear-eyed look at what the sector lacks: financial service providers that are capable, willing, and equipped to design products that fit the people they are supposed to serve. Banks and microfinance institutions in Iraq today mostly offer standardised products with high collateral requirements and limited digital capabilities. Reaching women led small businesses, rural communities, or young entrepreneurs running green or tech ventures requires a different kind of product, and often a different kind of institution. To bridge that gap, the project works directly with Iraqi financial service providers: banks, microfinance institutions, digital payment companies, fintechs, and government lending programmes. The approach combines needs assessments, hands-on advisory services, staff training, product design support, and pilot testing. The goal is not to deliver a finished product from outside, but to build the knowledge and process capacity within each institution so that change remains after the project ends. By the close of the assignment, at least three new or significantly adapted financial products must be in place, and these products must be actively reaching real users at a minimum of 950 individuals and 50 companies. The work also emphasises gender equality: women-led businesses are a priority target group, and all capacity-building activities must include a meaningful share of women participants. The broader context matters too. Iraq's Central Bank launched the national financial inclusion strategy that encourages digital payments, SME lending, and consumer protection improvements. ProDIGI project aligns directly with those priorities, making it both a practical intervention at the level of individual institutions and a contribution to the country's wider financial sector development. The selected firm will work directly with three to five financial service providers (FSPs) operating in Iraq. These may include commercial banks, microfinance institutions, digital payment providers, fintechs, and government lending schemes. GIZ will have pre-selected up to two FSPs before the contract starts, so work can begin without delay. The remaining FSPs will be selected by the contractor and GIZ jointly, based on agreed criteria.

title: Pipetting robot - 202511
description: The Norwegian Institute of Marine Research, department Molecular Biology Laboratory in Bergen, shall procure a flexible pipetting robot (liquid handler-robot, LH). The instrument shall be integrated in our production line for genotyping with next-generation sequencing (NGS), which is based on two stage PCR methodology. Thus the instrument will primarily be used for the construction of the NGS libraries and preparation of these for sequencing. The tasks that the instrument shall carry out include: i) Transferring DNA-templat, as well as adding master mixers and primers. ii) Cleaning PCR products (e.g. magnetic bullets) iii) Automated ("hands-off") quantification of DNA iv) Individual normalisation of libraries based on DNA concentration v) Merging of libraries The planned flow is 20,000– 30,000 samples per annum in a sample flow that will normally be carried out in 4 x 96 well plates with a reaction volume of 5-20 uL. In the future we envisage that 384 well plates will be a part of the test flow. As the instrument shall be used post-PCR, it is important that the instrument design allows effective cleaning and thorough decontamination. We would like a quick instrument with high capacity, pipetting precision and accuracy - even at low reaction volumes. In addition the robot is required to have great flexibility and an intuitive user interface, so that applications can be created and modified by personnel without advanced programming competence.

title: 10021316-Lot 1: Strengthening MSME Competitiveness, Market Access and Business Environment Reform in Benin
description: Benin's economy has experienced strong growth in recent years, with GDP growth estimated at around 6-7% annually. Nevertheless, this growth has not translated sufficiently into sustainable employment and income opportunities for the majority of the population. Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), which represent more than 95% of registered businesses in Benin, continue to face major structural constraints limiting their competitiveness, productivity and job creation potential. These constraints include limited access to finance and markets, low levels of innovation and digitalisation, weak managerial and technical capacities, insufficient quality infrastructure, and a mismatch between labour market needs and available skills. The project "Employment-oriented promotion of the competitiveness of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises" (ProPME 2) aims to improve the competitiveness of MSMEs in selected sectors and regions in Benin with a strong employment impact. The project focuses particularly on enterprises operating in the agri-food sector, renewable energies, crafts and services, as well as on strengthening entrepreneurial ecosystems and labour market intermediation structures. Particular attention is given to women-led enterprises and young entrepreneurs. The project contributes to Benin"s National Development Plan 2018-2025, the national SME promotion strategy and the national employment promotion strategy. It is implemented as part of the wider programme "Improvement of income and employment situation in Benin", jointly supported by German Development Cooperation through GIZ and KfW. In addition, the project supports the implementation of the Alliance for Product Quality in Africa (AfPQ), a multi-actor initiative implemented by GIZ and PTB to improve product quality and market access under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). The module is structured around three main outputs: - Output 1 aims to strengthen the entrepreneurial, technical and market integration capacities of MSMEs through tailored training, coaching and quality management support. - Output 2 aims to improve the business environment and strengthen support institutions involved in MSME development, quality infrastructure and public-private dialogue. - Output 3 aims to improve labour market intermediation and the alignment between vocational training and the skills needs of MSMEs.

description: Benin's economy is experiencing sustained economic growth, with real GDP growth estimated at around 6.4 % in 2023 and projected to remain above 6 % over the coming years. Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), which represent more than 95 % of registered enterprises, continue to face structural constraints including low productivity, weak integration into markets and value chains, limited access to finance and skilled labour, insufficient digitalisation, and inadequate business support services. Women-led enterprises and enterprises located in northern regions are particularly affected by these challenges. The Government of Benin has adopted several national strategies to strengthen economic productivity, employment promotion and SME competitiveness, including the National Development Plan 2018-2025, the national SME promotion strategy, the national employment policy and the "Benin Alafia 2060" vision. In parallel, the country aims to strengthen labour market governance through improved labour market information systems and territorial employment promotion approaches. The Federal Republic of Germany supports Benin in the implementation of these reforms through, among others, the project "Employment-oriented promotion of the competitiveness of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises" (ProPME 2). The project aims to improve the competitiveness of MSMEs in selected sectors and regions with a positive impact on employment. It focuses on the food processing industry, renewable energies, crafts and services sectors, as well as employment promotion and labour market intermediation. The module is structured around three main outputs: Output 1 aims to strengthen the competitiveness and growth capacities of MSMEs through tailored support, coaching and training measures. Output 2 aims to improve framework conditions for MSMEs through strengthened cooperation mechanisms, institutional support and public-private dialogue. Output 3 aims to improve the conditions for the placement of qualified workers in MSMEs through strengthened employment governance, labour market intermediation and labour market information systems.

The project shall also analyse what factors contribute to immigrants coming in and staying in work, despite limited Norwegian proficiencies. The knowledge shall provide a better basis for understanding how language can function both as a door opener and barrier to participation in working life, and should be able to be used in policy development and to strengthen IMDi's guidance work and cooperation with employers, municipalities and other relevant actors. This can, among other things, contribute to more precise and flexible language requirements, clearer distinctions between oral and written skills and better adaptations of language requirements for specific work assignments. title: Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya
description: This Assignment is financed from official Danish development assistance through the Danish Africa Water facility (Danish Finance Act § 06.32.01.32). Emphasis is therefore on providing safe and affordable access to water for all (Sustainable Development Goal 6.1), increase water-use efficiency and ensure freshwater supplies (Sustainable Development Goal 6.4) and to raise capacity for planning and management of climate change (Sustainable Goal 13.5). The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Royal Danish Embassy, Nairobi (RDE) is the funding agency and Water Resources Authority (WRA) is the Recipient of the outcome of the Assignment. The Assignment aims at operating with a high level of local content by engaging local partners with the view of increasing the long-term sustainability of digital systems and ease of their future maintenance as well as enhanced dialogue on water use with local communities. The Water Resources Authority (WRA) is a state corporation established under Section 11 of the Water Act, 2016 and mandated to regulate the management and use of Kenya's water resources on behalf of the national government. WRA formulates standards and regulations, issues and enforces water permits, sets water-use fees, and advises the Cabinet Secretary on national water-resource policy. WRA operates through a decentralised structure comprising one head office, six basin offices, 26 sub-basins, eight laboratories and three satellite offices. WRA is currently undertaking the development of an Enterprise Architecture as part of the Government’s Digitization of Government Services Performance Contracting initiative, in alignment with the Government Enterprise Architecture framework and applicable Government ICT standards. Kenya has a comparatively clear formal water-resource governance architecture, but implementation is constrained by incomplete coordination across national, basin, county and sub-catchment levels, limited basin and sub-basin resources, and overlapping institutional interfaces. WRA already operates digital permitting, e-billing, smart-metering, hydrological monitoring, GIS and laboratory systems; however, these features remains fragmented and have not yet been demonstrated to provide an end-to-end authoritative record linking the water user and abstraction point to the permit, meter, reading, invoice, payment, inspection and hydrological context. The core information-management challenge is not the absence of digital systems, but their fragmentation across field monitoring, permitting, metering, billing, enforcement and hydrological decision support. WRA is working to create integrations between its various IT solutions, but the vision for this project is to support components in establishing a single point of entry/IT solution—hereinafter referred to as WRIMS—that will ensure integration among all existing IT solutions, as shown in the diagram below and elaborated in the background document on WRA’s existing IT environment. The Assignment regarding Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya (hereafter “IMPRODATWRM”) is expected to be designed to close the institutional and information-management gap while strengthening WRA's own-source revenue base and the evidence available for sustainable allocation. The Assignment is to support WRA in transforming its fragmented digital landscape into an integrated, interoperable WRIMS environment that connects the full operating chain - from registration and permitting through meter/device management, reliable measurement, validation, billing, payment reconciliation, inspection and enforcement, and will connect these regulatory transactions to basin-level hydrological information. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. The Assignment will align with and leverage the resulting business, data, application, technology and security architectures to guide the design and implementation of WRIMS, while supporting the operationalisation of the EA, particularly in systems integration, interoperability, data governance, ICT infrastructure and cybersecurity. The Assignment is divided into three phases: Phase I: Detailed verification, system analysis and preparation Phase II: A Kenyan-led option assessment and decision Phase III: Design, build, test, roll-out and stabilised operation

title: Shesknan Bridge Works
description: The project involves the replacement/rehabilitation of a single-span road bridge in poor structural condition and has partially collapsed. Works will focus on the replacement of bridge deck and parapet walls, abutment and wingwall re-pointing, vegetation clearance, and associated ancillary works. Shesknan Bridge is a single-span masonry arch bridge of approximately 6m span, supporting a local road crossing over a natural watercourse. The bridge consists of a masonry arch barrel, stone sidewalls and parapets, with a relatively shallow depth of fill material supporting the road surface above. The recommended solution for the bridge is full replacement. This addresses advanced deterioration including reinforcement corrosion, section loss and spalling, which render repair-only strategies uneconomical and short-lived. Additional works are anticipated to include the following:  Site mobilisation and establishment.  Temporary works and access provision.  Demolition of defective components.  Parapet, abutment and wingwall works.  Vegetation clearance and habitat measures.  Road reinstatement, surfacing and safety barrier installation.  Final inspection and handover.
